claims.text: The selected Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quaternary and ternary derivatives are single-phase FCC after the specified thermomechanical processing.
Changing the number of constituents in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived alloys changes their short-range chemical order and nanoscale clustering.
Short-range chemical order alters the local lattice-potential landscape.
Changes in the local lattice-potential landscape alter dislocation nucleation.
Changes in the local lattice-potential landscape alter dislocation glide.
Local chemical ordering can produce dislocation-pinning sites or regions that facilitate slip.
SRO-mediated changes in dislocation nucleation and glide govern differences in yield strength.
SRO-mediated changes in dislocation nucleation and glide govern differences in ductility.
Identical rolling and annealing treatments will isolate composition-related SRO as the cause of mechanical-property differences.
High-resolution TEM and atom-probe tomography can quantify the relevant nanoscale SRO or clustering metrics.
Alloys with fewer constituent elements will have measurably different SRO heterogeneity than the equiatomic quinary alloy.
Enhanced SRO clustering may increase yield strength.
Enhanced SRO clustering may reduce ductility.
Reduced SRO heterogeneity may lower yield strength.
Reduced SRO heterogeneity may enhance ductility.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when secondary phases or processing-induced microstructural differences are present.
Grain size or precipitate formation may contribute to deformation behavior independently of SRO.
A lack of statistically significant association between SRO metrics and yield strength or ductility across the variants would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions assert that identical processing ensures composition-related SRO is solely responsible for property differences, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that grain size, precipitates, and processing nuances may also govern deformation. Identical processing does not itself ensure identical resulting microstructures across different compositions.
